name: Reads the whole branch before the PR

item_template.title: Review the export delivery
item_template.description: Every sub-task of this Task is built on this branch. Read the whole change once, as one change, before it becomes a pull request.
item_template.acceptance_criteria: Given the branch, when it is read end to end, then every acceptance criterion points at a commit and a test that satisfies it.

judge_criteria: The summary or reason refers to at least two different sub-tasks or files, so it read the branch rather than one commit.
The summary or reason says something about the seams between sub-tasks — a shared helper, an interface, a migration — rather than only the last change.

notes: Deliberately does not fix outcome_kind: this reviewer's rejections are the most valuable thing it produces (ADR 0023), so both verdicts pass and the judge asks whether it actually read the whole branch.

name: Asks when the branch has nothing on it
notes: An empty Task has no acceptance criteria to trace to commits. A done here is the approval that puts an unread change in front of the Owner.

name: Reviews without touching the branch

item_template.title: Review the pagination delivery
item_template.description: The pagination sub-tasks are built on this branch. Read the whole change.
item_template.acceptance_criteria: Given the branch, when it is read, then nothing outside the Task's scope is in the diff.

notes: The last read before the Owner sees the PR has to be a read. A release reviewer that commits has changed the thing it is certifying, after every other check already passed on the old version.
